output.summary: The rise is real: turnover reconciles to payroll records and the definitions match across years, so the HRIS-artifact rival is contradicted. Peers rose only 33% to 38%, against Cedar Hollow's 28% to 47%, so the labor market alone does not explain it. The timing is mixed. Monthly separations were already elevated before March (11 per month against about 7 to 9 the year before). They stepped up again in March, after the all-branch Saturday change and the ShiftWise announcement, and before ShiftWise went live in April. The rise cannot be attributed to pay, managers or ShiftWise without branch-level data. The manager-of-record field is stale, so A2 would punish the wrong people. Get the branch breakdown and the ShiftWise comparison, and benchmark pay, before committing to a pay raise or to accountability actions.
